# Workflow Station Guidelines (English bundle)

Portal: /help/. Audience: designers. Not source code.

## Computed field formulas (/help/computed-fields)

A computed column fills itself. People cannot type into it on forms. Save uses the server formula engine. Formula dialog Calculate is preview only.

Order: open Table Design and the table → tick Computed → open Formula → save the table.

Screenshot table: Purchase Request, help_pr. Computed: window_days, line_count, grand_total, over_budget. Sub-table help_pr_line has line_total = quantity * unit_price.

Samples:
- This row: quantity * unit_price
- Related rows (main table only): SUM(help_pr_line.line_total), COUNT(help_pr_line)
- Sub-table reads main: help_pr.request_title (column must not itself be computed; do not wrap in SUM)
- Dates: end_date - start_date ; DATEDIFF(start_date, end_date)
- Logic: IF(grand_total > 5000, "Y", "N")

Result type must match Data Type. Fail: block save shows #ERR; leave blank saves the rest of the form with this column empty.

Admin Relation Tables are standalone: no MAIN/SUB lookup, no SUM related-row functions. See /help/computed-fields#relation.

## Tables, fields, PK and FK (/help/table-design)

Function Unit tab Table Design. Create MAIN / SUB / ACTION / RELATION tables. Field Name must start with a letter. Import Table Fields on Form Design reads these columns. Attach tables to a form in /help/table-bindings. Views need a Main Table first.

Order: open Table Design → create or open a table → add fields → tick Primary Key and pick a strategy → tick Foreign Key and set Ref Table → save. On a MAIN table configure Request ID first.

PK strategies: UUID, Manual, Auto increment, Prefixed sequence, Date + daily sequence, Date + monthly sequence, Custom format. Primary Key cannot stay nullable.

SLA Due Date (#sla-due-date, MAIN only, optional): Configure on the SLA Due Date row → Start date source (Main table field: pick a DATE/TIMESTAMP Start date field; or Submission time) → Due date field (non-formula DATE, read-only on forms) → Confirm → Save the table. Remove clears the mapping. Renaming the mapped field in the grid carries the mapping along; deleting it blocks Save with "SLA field does not exist on this table". The lead time in days is set in Admin Center (/help/sla-policies).

Related: /help/computed-fields , /help/table-bindings , /help/view-design , /help/sla-policies

## Manage Table Bindings (/help/table-bindings)

Form Design toolbar Manage Table Bindings. Dialog title Table Binding Management. Attaches MAIN / SUB / ACTION / RELATION tables to this form. Not the Sub-Table grid (/help/form-ctl-sub-table). Lookup reads Relation Table bindings (/help/form-ctl-lookup).

Screenshot tables: Purchase Request PRIMARY help_pr, SUB help_pr_line. Do not invent a second FK on help_pr_line.

Order: open Form Design → Edit this form → Manage Table Bindings → Add Binding (type, table, Filter foreign key for Sub Table) → Add → Close → save the form → Sub Table Binding on the canvas picks that SUB.

List columns: Table Name, Binding Type, Mode, Foreign Key Field, Link Mode, Sub Mode, Operations. Empty list: No table bindings. Primary cannot be deleted.

Add Binding fields: Binding Type (Primary Table / Sub Table / Action Table / Relation Table); Sub Mode Full Mode (Form + List) or Form Only Mode; Select Table; Binding Mode Editable / Read Only; Link Mode Structural FK or MI Participant Row; Filter foreign key; Participant Row Field.

Foreign-key fill source (Structural FK Sub Table, after Select Table): Auto (unique table only) / Host / parent row / Primary form / Named ancestor binding + Select ancestor binding.

Same SUB table twice only when Filter foreign key differs. Primary and Relation stay one per table.

Fail: Add a Primary first; A primary binding already exists; A conflicting table binding already exists; No structural FK fields; Select which declared foreign key; Please select a table; Primary table binding cannot be deleted.

Related: /help/table-design , /help/form-ctl-sub-table , /help/form-ctl-lookup

## View Design (/help/view-design)

Published list of one table. Access control decides who sees it in User Portal.

Order: Main Table exists → open View Design → select or Create view / Generate default views → add columns → Name, Export, Detail form, Access control, Sort / Filter → save.

Access (#access): empty Business Units and Roles → nobody sees the view after publishing. If you configure access, pick at least one Business Unit and at least one Role. A user must match both in the current Business Unit and Role. System Administrator is checked the same way as everyone else, for views and for rows (Only involved users see data applies to everyone).

Related: /help/table-design , /help/form-ctl-lookup

## Send email (/help/email-send)

Three pieces: Outbound connection, Email Template, Send Task. Subject and body live on the template, not the node.

Order: Outbound connection → template (enabled) → Send Task → To + Connection + Template → save.

SMTP host/port/TLS come from Admin Center → System Config (not typed on the connection form). Same email cannot have two connections in the same direction.

Connection fields: Direction (Outbound send / Inbound monitor); Sender Email (From address, required, also the name); Sender Display Name (optional); Username / Password (SMTP login; password required when username set; blank on edit keeps stored); SMTP Host, Port, Use TLS (Admin System Config); Email Provider (list column); Enabled; Test / Test Recipient / Send Test Email.

Template fields: Template Name (required); Subject (Insert Variable, empty after fill fails send); Insert Variable (main / Lookup / sub-table table); Body; Visual / HTML; Email preview (design-time); Enabled (required for send).

Send Task fields: To (required, address or ${fieldName}; multiple addresses semicolon-separated); Insert field button (main-table ${fieldName} only, plus initiator); Connection (required outbound); From override (optional); Template (required); Basic Info Task ID / Type / Task Name. Advanced: Cc, Bcc, Attachments (FILE Upload field), Sensitivity (Normal/Personal/Private/Confidential), Reply-To, Importance (Low/Normal/High).

Template example: PR Approved Notice. Failures: missing/inbound/disabled connection; empty To; missing/disabled template; empty subject after variables; attachment not FILE; no global SMTP; instance started before Deploy or user task after the Send Task not completed first.

Related: /help/action-email , /help/email-monitor , /help/computed-fields , /help/form-upload

## Send email after this Action (/help/action-email)

Optional mail on one Action Design button. Portal sends only after that Action succeeds. Connection and template are the same as /help/email-send.

Order: Outbound connection → enabled Email Template → Action Design → Edit Action → Send email after success → To + Email connection + Email template → save → bind Action to the user task → run that Action in Portal.

Fields: Send email after this Action (section); Send email after success (off = no mail); To (required when on; address or ${initiator}; { } Insert field / Search fields…); Email connection (required when on; Outbound or Both); Email template (required when on; Enabled only); Show / Hide advanced; From, Cc, Bcc (optional); Attachments (optional FILE-field picker, same as Send Task emailAttachments).

Types that send: Approve, Reject, Transfer, Delegate, Urge, Rollback, Withdraw, Draft, Save, Process Submit, Process Reject, Form Popup. API Call, Custom Script, Composite Action show “Portal does not execute this Action type, so it will not send email” and block save if the switch is on.

Failures: missing To / connection / template; unsupported type; empty connection or template list; Action not bound to the user task; Portal save that is not this Action button.

Related: /help/email-send#connection , /help/email-send#template , /help/email-send#send-task

## Allowed Roles (/help/action-allowed-roles)

Who sees an Action button in Portal. Open Function Unit → Action Design → Edit. The field is under Visibility & Permissions. Select one or more business roles (business-unit-bound, or not bound to a business unit). The dropdown shows the role name and stores the role code. Admin and developer roles are not listed. A saved code that left the catalog still shows as that code.

Empty means every portal user sees the button. Portal hides the button on the task page and the start page unless the session holds at least one listed code. The session is the current workspace role plus roles that are not bound to a business unit. System Administrator gets no exception and is not in the dropdown.

This hides the button only. A direct call with a valid session can still run the Action.

Related: /help/action-email

## Email Monitor (/help/email-monitor)

Starts a process when mail arrives.

Order: Inbound connection → monitor template → bind sample text to main-table fields → Inbound Email Trigger on Start event → save binding → Deploy.

Inbound connection fields: Direction Inbound; Mailbox Email (required, also the name); IMAP Username / Password; IMAP Host, Port, SSL from Admin System Config; Enabled.

Monitor template fields: Rule Name (required); Inbound Mailbox (required); System Initiator (optional search); Folder / Label (blank → INBOX); Poll Interval seconds (min 30); Send to manual review when required fields are missing; Enabled is list-only (new rules start enabled). Do not set Process Key, From Filter, or Subject Filter on the template.

Extraction wizard: Sample Email (Subject, From, Plain Text Body, HTML Body); Field Mapping (Add Field, Bind selection, Target Field, Source: Subject / Text+HTML recommended / Text+HTML / HTML only / Header / Constant; Method: LABEL BETWEEN REGEX CONST HEADER; Rule; Required; Preview); Sub-table HTML table (Add Sub-table, Sub Table Binding, Table # 0-based, Table selector, First row is header, Add Column, Column #).

Start Event fields: Start process when email arrives; Process Key (auto); Start Event ID (auto); Email Monitor template (required when on); Inbound Mailbox (read-only); Field extraction status; From Filter; Subject Filter (example Quote); Save Start Event binding.

Examples: template Vendor quote to PR; folder INBOX; extraction to request_title; Subject Filter Quote on StartEvent_Email.

Every enabled monitor template must be bound before Deploy. Bound templates cannot be deleted until unbound.

Related: /help/email-send#connection , /help/computed-fields

## To Do — claim pool (/help/up-tasks-to-claim)

To Do lists direct assignments and business-unit role requests (free, held by you, held by a colleague) on one page. Role-pool requests, free or held (yours included), are listed only while the header workspace is that business unit and role; switching workspace hides them until you switch back. The task page itself opens in any workspace (for example from an email link). Claim before edit. Claim all (top right) confirms once then claims every free request in batches of 100. After a search, tick rows: Claim and Unclaim sit between “N selected” and Batch Urge, stay visible, and disable when none of the ticks can be claimed or released; confirm shows “N of M selected”. Unclaim all releases only your holds; it never force-unclaims a colleague. Auto-claim on open (To Do and User Profile, stored with the account, default off) claims a free role request when you click its Request ID on To Do only — not Home, notifications, or Completed Tasks. Assignment Type uses a distinct colour per category; the filter no longer includes Virtual Group (use BU + role). /tasks/to-claim redirects here.

Order: open To Do → Claim, Claim all, or Unclaim all → edit and submit.

While the holder still has Portal access, a Leader of that business unit and role, or the business-unit Approver, can Release Claim on someone else’s hold (confirm first) or Reassign the request to another member of the same role. System Administrator gets no exception; Auditor cannot. Release Claim returns the request to the pool; Reassign does not. Member cannot. Apply Permission on User Profile Setup chooses Member or Leader for that BU+Role. Change History and Admin Center User Portal Audit Log record claim, unclaim, release claim, and reassign (who / when / from / to); Take over is recorded as Reassign.

Lost access, leaving, role changes (#lost-access): a person loses Portal access when their account is disabled or locked, or they are in no group that grants Portal access. On a pool request they hold, To Do and the task banner show Assignee has lost Portal access; any other pool member with Portal access can Release Claim, Take over (confirm; you become the holder), or Reassign to another pool member with access. On the To Do row: Take over plus a More menu holding Release Claim and Reassign (each only when allowed); the task-page claim banner shows all three. The banner appears on BU + role requests, and on named-list requests whenever you can act on them. Pool = the business unit and role (BU + role request), or the list of named people. A request assigned to one person whose account is still active does not move; they request Portal access again. A person has left when an administrator disables or deletes the account (locked is not left): their directly assigned requests, and pool requests they held where nobody else in the pool has access, go automatically to their Entity Manager, else Function Manager (manager must be active with Portal access); the request appears on the manager’s To Do and is handled or transferred like any other. Neither manager available → the request stays; administrators fix the manager data. A free request for named people goes to a manager only once all of them left; a free BU + role request waits in its pool. A manager with access but no business role still receives it and works it after getting a role. BU + role pools follow grants: a new grant joins that pair’s open pool requests right away (including older ones); a revoked grant leaves them and its holds go back to the pool. Change History shows System as Changed By: Reassigned to manager (Claimed By · Reassigned by the system: the assignee has left) and Release Claim (Claimed By · Released: the holder no longer holds this BU + Role). Setup → Delegations: a standing rule shows Not in effect: the delegator / the delegate has lost Portal access and does not apply until access is back; the rule is not deleted. A single-task Delegate from the task page (/help/task-delegate) follows the same rule: the delegate stops seeing it under To Do → Delegated, the task stays with the delegator, and the Delegated to line on Basic Info adds the same Not in effect text. A single-task delegation ends for good when the task changes hands (Unclaim / Release Claim, Take over, Reassign, the system's release or reassignment to a manager); Change History adds Delegation ended with Delegated to · Ended: the task changed hands (Old Value = the delegate); the new holder can delegate again.

## Delegate a task (/help/task-delegate)

You are Current Assignee. Delegate this one open task. You stay the assignee. Someone else can complete it on your behalf.

This is not Transfer (that button still changes the assignee). This is not Setup → Delegations standing rules. Both kinds stop applying while the delegator or the delegate has lost Portal access (see /help/up-tasks-to-claim#lost-access): the delegate no longer sees the task under To Do → Delegated and cannot complete it; the task stays in the delegator's name and the delegator can complete it; the line reads Delegated to X · Not in effect: the delegate has lost Portal access (or the delegator); the delegation is not deleted and applies again once access is back. With a BU+Role target, a member of that pair who has no Portal access cannot complete it on the delegator's behalf; the pair as a whole never counts as having lost access, so when nobody in it can complete the task the task stays with the delegator, who completes it as usual; the pair as a whole is never marked Not in effect, and only the delegator's Not in effect line can show, when the delegator has lost Portal access. The delegation belongs to the current holder and ends as soon as the hold ends or the task moves to someone else (Unclaim or Release Claim, Take over, Reassign by a Leader, Approver or pool member, a system release after the holder lost the BU + Role, or the system passing it to the manager of a holder who left): the delegate no longer sees it under To Do → Delegated, the Delegated to line disappears, and Change History adds Delegation ended with Delegated to · Ended: the task changed hands (Old Value = the delegate; Changed By = whoever released, took over or reassigned, or System). It does not come back by itself; the new holder can delegate again.

Order: open the task from To Do → click Delegate → choose Specified user or Specified BU and Role → Confirm → the other person opens Delegated on To Do.

Specified user: click Target User (Click to search). Table columns Username, Display Name, Full Name, Email, Employee ID; type to search on the server; pick a row. Extra line Delegated to that person. They see On behalf of you. You can still complete it yourself.

Specified BU and Role: pick Business Unit then Role (both required; Role disabled until a unit is chosen). Visible and completable only when the header workspace is that same pair. Switching workspace hides it. System Administrator does not see every delegated task. No Claim after this kind of delegate.

Unclaimed pool: Delegate is hidden until someone is assigned. Delegate shows only on tasks that can be delegated; some tasks do not offer it.

Failures: Please select user; Please select both business unit and role; cannot delegate to yourself; completed tasks cannot be delegated; This task cannot be delegated: delegation is not available for it.

## Form Design — Advanced Upload (/help/form-upload)

Advanced Upload is in the Extend palette. New fields default to Single (one file, saved as a URL for Activepieces File / send-email). Turn on Multi to set Max files (default 10 when turned on, 2–50). Default Max file size is 10MB; the platform hard cap is 50MB. Saved JSON that still has Multiple off + Limit 1 and no Max files was a generator default; those fields still accept up to 10 until the switch is changed. The properties panel shows Multi and Max file size. Basic palette Upload stays the stock form-create control.

Order: in Table Design add a FILE column → in Form Design Import Table Fields, or set the Advanced Upload Field to that column name → leave Multi off or turn it on and set Max files → set Max file size → save → check Preview or User Portal on that same form. Dragging from Extend does not add a table column. If My Request or To Do must show the same files, open that scene’s form, click Add Advanced Upload from New Request (copies the same Field onto the main canvas and matching sub-tables), then Save. Portal does not invent the widget at runtime.

Each scene is its own canvas. New Request, My Request, and To Do each have a separate form design. The widget Field must be a Table Design FILE column (same as Basic Upload, e.g. fileupload). A palette drop that still has a generated F… Field will not show files already stored on a real column.

Properties: Multi switch (off = Single / one file; on = Max files 2–50, default 10). Max file size (default 10MB, 1–50, platform cap 50MB). No stock Maximum number of uploads allowed; Multi plus Max files is the only count cap. At most 3 uploads run at once. One stored file is a URL; two or more are a JSON array of url and name.

Runtime: when Multi is off, drop or pick one file. When Multi is on, drop several files onto the dashed box, or click it and multi-select in the file picker (Ctrl/Shift). Files appear as name-sorted cards inside the box; click a card for File details. Preview is next to the file name; Download is there unless Can not download is on. File Description saves only when you click Save. Callback URL and Auto Send to FileNet are hidden for now. Sub-table cell shows report.pdf +2; companion filename column joins names with "; ". Send Email FILE attachments include every stored file. Basic Upload uses the same drawer.

Failures: Maximum {limit} files allowed; file over Max file size is rejected; submit/save blocked while a file is uploading or failed; session expiry (401) asks you to sign in and upload again; zip is skipped from the in-form preview playlist.

Related: /help/email-send#send-task

## Form events (/help/form-events)

Two places to write scripts: Edit on a selected control, and Form event on the Form tab (button still Edit). Not Table Design Formula.

Sidebar: Form Design → Controls → How to write events. Click a control name under Basic / Extend / MI / Layout / Auxiliary — there is no Event item under each control.

Order: open Form Design → select a control (or open Form tab → Form event) → Edit → Create / pick a name → Save → Ok → save the form.

The Edit dialog has Create on the left and the script editor on the right. Grey text next to each function is when it runs. Save writes the function you are editing. Ok keeps the list. Footer Cancel discards dialog edits.

When each Create event runs (/help/form-events#when):
- change: Input/Textarea after blur or Enter if the text changed; Select/Radio/Checkbox/Date/Switch as soon as the chosen value changes
- blur / focus: this control loses or gains focus
- click: listed on layout, Auxiliary, and shells (Inline Form, Record Note, Assignment Mode)
- hook_load: after this control’s rules are loaded (form first appears)
- hook_mounted: after this control is on the page (later than hook_load)
- hook_deleted: after this control’s rules are removed
- hook_watch: after this control’s rules change (not the field value)
- hook_value: after this control’s stored value changes (Input change still waits for blur/Enter)
- hook_hidden: after show/hide (hidden / display)
- hook_titleClick: field label click, not the control body
- Custom: only a name this control actually emits

Extra names (removeTag, calendarChange, …) are on that control’s page.

Shared names in every control event: $inject, api (same as options), value, field, formData (same snapshot as data), user, option (often empty), rule/self (rarely needed), args (original payload). Always write user && before a property.

Each method on the human page is written as: if you want X, use this; before (designer default); after (what you see). This index keeps method names for lookup.

api (same methods on Form event via api / options):
- getValue(field) / setValue(field, value) / setValue({ field: value, … }) / api.form (read snapshot; do not assign)
- setValue second-argument shape lives on each control’s Events section (/help/form-ctl-input#events …). Hub index: /help/form-events#set-shapes. Sub-Table: /help/form-ctl-sub-table. Lookup: /help/form-ctl-lookup. Owner / Link Form: /help/form-events-extend. Advanced Upload: /help/form-upload. Clear text with ''; clear a list with [].
- required(true|false, field) / requiredStatus(field)
- disabled(true|false, field) / disabledStatus(field) — whole-form readonly and audit fields stay locked
- hidden(true) removes from page (not submitted); hidden(false) puts back; hiddenStatus — also Card/Tabs/Collapse/Row
- display(true) hides with CSS; display(false) shows; displayStatus is true when shown
- setOptions / addOption / removeOption / clearOptions / resetOptions — Select/Radio/Checkbox only; clearOptions does not clear the field value
- setFieldError / clearFieldError — blocks Save until cleared; beforeSubmit return false also blocks Save
- setFormNotification(message, ERROR|WARNING|INFO, uniqueId) / clearFormNotification — ERROR banner does not block Save
- setLookupFilter / clearLookupFilter / refresh — Lookup only (field is that control’s Field name); AND with designer/cascade; invalid selection auto-clears. No Sub-Table refresh
- setFocus / setLabel / getLabel / resetLabel — labels are plain text
Omit field on hidden/display/required/disabled only to affect every field.

Samples use help_pr / help_pr_line (request_title, requester, scenario, start_date, end_date, cost_center, notes, quantity).

Hooks on every control: hook_load, hook_mounted, hook_deleted, hook_watch, hook_value, hook_hidden, hook_titleClick.

Form event names: onSubmit, onReset, onCreated, onMounted, onReload, onChange, beforeSubmit, beforeFetch. onChange has field, value, options. beforeSubmit can return false to stop Save.

Form Preview has no Portal workspace: activeBusinessUnitName and activeRoleName stay empty until User Portal.

Per-control events: /help/form-events-basic (Basic index), then /help/form-ctl-input and each Basic control; /help/form-ctl-sub-table and /help/form-ctl-lookup; /help/form-events-extend (remaining Extend + MI), /help/form-events-layout (Layout + Auxiliary).

Related: /help/computed-fields

## Basic (/help/form-events-basic)

Palette group Basic. Each control is /help/form-ctl-<type> (Input, Textarea, Password, InputNumber, Radio, Checkbox, Select, Switch, Slider, Rate, Date, DateRange, Time, TimeRange, Cascader, ColorPicker, Upload, Tree, TreeSelect, Transfer, Editor). Old hashes /help/form-events-basic#input redirect to the control article. Field catalog is on that control’s page. One event sample per control; full api methods on /help/form-events. Control pages must say what the control looks like and what the Field stores — Radio shows every option and stores one value key; Checkbox stores a key array; Select hides options until opened.

## Extend and MI events (/help/form-events-extend)

Index for remaining Extend and MI shells. Sub-Table is /help/form-ctl-sub-table (bound SUB grid, help_pr_line, Allow Add/Edit/Delete). Attach the table in /help/table-bindings first. Lookup is /help/form-ctl-lookup (Relation Table, filters, cascade, Backfill; setLookupFilter then refresh). This page keeps one event sample for Inline Form, Link Form, Owner, Record Note, and Assignment Mode. Old hashes /help/form-events-extend#subTable and #lookup redirect to those articles.

Sub-Table batch operations: /help/form-ctl-sub-table#batch. Select rows in the outer grid before Batch Edit; the dialog renders the saved Batch Form layout, styles and control properties without internal row selection or extra field-intent controls. Untouched fields remain unchanged, including displayed designer defaults. Enter a value once to set all selected rows; zero and false are values. Emptying a field through its configured control explicitly clears it; Cancel and reopen discards the draft. PK/FK/calculated fields remain protected. Assignment Mode provides its intrinsic person/BU/Role pickers from the frozen sub-table assignment contract, including marker-only existing forms. Authored child rules preserve labels/styles; configured field names, never name conventions, identify the pickers. No selected mode leaves assignment unchanged; clicking the active card deselects it. Changed person or BU+Role targets must be complete; clearing assignment is not supported. Batch Add is a separate command: fill once and request 1–200 new rows, with generated keys and configured FK prepared on Apply. Batch Delete confirms the outer selection. Apply updates the page; normal Save or auto-save must succeed. Existing instance capabilities and permissions stay frozen.

New Request rechecks the published batch design on Submit Application. If it changed while the page was open, submission is blocked before process creation; refresh the form and check the restored draft before resubmitting. Existing instances retain their own batch design.
Assignment warnings after submission or task completion mean the action has already happened: do not repeat it. Open My Requests → application detail → Flow History for saved verification results and affected task IDs. Records describe the submission/completion time, not current task status. A record-save failure is shown separately; contact an administrator. Saving assignment values alone does not prove task creation.
Form Preview uses the same outer-row selection and one Batch Form. Batch Add works on an empty grid without inventing sample records. Apply changes only preview data; Cancel discards pending values. Preview does not save business data or create tasks.

## Layout and Auxiliary events (/help/form-events-layout)

Usually click plus hooks. Tabs may also list tabClick, tabChange, tabAdd, tabRemove when Create shows those names. Button click can fill requester from user.

## Requirements and Function Unit Design (/help/fu-documents)

Every Function Unit keeps two Markdown documents, Requirements and Function Unit Design, edited in Function Unit Settings. Each Save adds a version. AI Studio reads both and updates them after a phase is confirmed.

Order: open the Function Unit → Function Unit Settings → Requirements or Function Unit Design tab → type Markdown or Import a file → check the preview → Save.

Toolbar: Edit (two panes), Preview (rendered only; read-only members always), Import, Download, Version History, Save, Unsaved tag, version line (version · saver · time · source), No document yet.

Import accepts .md, .markdown, .txt up to 200 KB and only loads the editor; nothing is stored until Save. With unsaved changes a dialog asks (Replace / Cancel). Download writes what the editor shows; file name example Purchase_Request-requirements-v1.2.md.

Version History: Current tag, View, Compare with current, Restore (adds a new version with the old text). Sources: Manual edit, Imported, Cloned, Restored from v1.1, Rolled back to version 1.0.2, AI Studio · <phase> confirmed, AI Studio · full check, AI Studio · one-click generation. The number before the dot goes up when a new AI design is started in AI Studio; the number after the dot on every Save.

Export carries both documents; importing adds them as a version marked Imported; Clone copies the latest text; a Version Management rollback writes that version's documents back. Older packages leave documents unchanged.

Fail: wrong file type; file or document larger than 200 KB; empty file; Document changed (Load latest / Save anyway); read-only members have no Import, Save, Restore.

Related: /help/ai-studio

## Build with AI (AI Studio) (/help/ai-studio)

The AI Studio button on a Function Unit opens Build with AI. Three modes: Start a new AI design (phase by phase with the copilot; asks before resetting existing progress), Continue AI draft (disabled until someone confirmed a phase or talked to the copilot), One-click generate. Read-only members do not see the button. AI Studio has eleven phases in designer-tab order, Process Design to Validation.

One-click generate (#one-click). Order: AI Studio → One-click generate → describe what the Function Unit should do (up to 4000 characters; optional when a Requirements document exists, otherwise Generate is disabled) → Generate → Replace the current design? → Generate. The description, the current design and both documents go to the model. One round writes process, tables and relations, forms, actions, decisions. It does not write views, connections, email templates, email monitors or automation bindings.

Result (#result): AI Studio opens on Process Design and waits, usually 7 to 15 minutes; Stop cancels without changing the design; the page can be reloaded or left. The Proposed change card groups items by phase (new N, replaces N existing). Applied means the design is written and the designers reloaded. Apply appears when it was generated but not written. Let AI fix it appears when the card lists errors and runs the whole generation again. The description is saved as a new Requirements version (source AI Studio · one-click generation; appended under Additional requirements when text existed). Phase progress returns to Process Design; review each phase and click Confirm phase.

Fail: Generate disabled without description or Requirements document; AI credentials are missing, please sign in again; errors on the card mean nothing was written; a warning that it could not be applied automatically → click Apply; a red copilot message means the round failed and the design is unchanged; no Undo, roll back in Version Management.

Related: /help/fu-documents , /help/table-design , /help/view-design , /help/email-send

## SLA Policies (/help/sla-policies)

Admin Center → SLA Policies. Due date = start date + lead time (calendar days). Fields are mapped in Table Design (/help/table-design#sla-due-date); the lead time is set here per Function Unit and per environment, never exported with the Function Unit.

Order: map fields in Developer Workstation and deploy → the Function Unit appears with Lead Time Not set → Edit, Lead Time (days) 1–3650 whole number, optional Change reason (≤500) → Save → Details.

Saving recalculates every open case (Running, Suspended) in the background; completed and withdrawn cases keep their due date. Recalculate re-runs it with the current lead time. Job statuses: Pending, Running, Succeeded, Partial (some cases skipped or failed), Failed, Superseded (a newer save replaced it). Details: latest 20 jobs; per job up to 500 Updated / Skipped / Failed cases with Old Due Date, New Due Date, Reason; Change history of the latest 50 saves with Recalculation start Started / Pending / Failed to start.

Rules: Lead Time Not set → no due date, existing values stay. Start date empty or not a date → due date unchanged, case Skipped. The due date is written by the platform on submit and save and cannot be edited on forms.

Permissions (#permissions): System Administrator sees every Function Unit and can Edit and Recalculate all. Technical Lead sees only the Function Units of the teams they lead and can Edit and Recalculate those. Auditor sees every Function Unit read-only (Details, Export). An Auditor who also leads a team changes that team's. A Function Unit without a team in Admin Center is listed only for System Administrator and Auditor.

Related: /help/table-design#sla-due-date , /help/environment-variables

## Node action order (/help/node-action-order)
In Process Design, select a user task and expand Actions. Select Available Actions and drag rows by their name/handle or use Move up/down in Button display order. Each completed drag is one undo/redo operation; read-only units cannot be reordered. Top-to-bottom becomes left-to-right in Portal. New selections append; removals preserve survivors. Save the process and publish/deploy. Each node has an independent order. Process global actions follow node actions; globals appear in a separate read-only group without sorting or removal; legacy duplicates appear once in the global group. Action Design Bound Nodes shows only Process Global for a global action. Allowed Roles filtering preserves survivor order. Existing instances use their bound version.


## New Requests (/help/up-new)

Choose a request card to open its form. Only workflows available in your current workspace are listed. Open Request → New Requests. Search for the workflow or choose a card from Favorites. Select the card, complete the form and use its submit action. Use the search field beside the page title to narrow the cards. Clear it to restore the list. Each card shows the workflow icon, name, description when provided, and version. Hover over a shortened name or description to read it in full. Favorites appears above the main grid when the returned list includes favorite workflows. A star marks these cards. They also remain in the main grid; either card opens the same request form. No matching requests means the search found no results: clear the search or try another keyword. No processes available means the workspace returned no accessible workflows. Check the selected Business Unit and Role, or contact your administrator about access. Choosing a card opens a form; it does not submit a request.

New Requests favorites: Select the outline star at the top right of a card to add it to Favorites. Select the filled star to remove it. The star does not open the request form. Both grids update after the server confirms the change, and favorites are saved for your account across refreshes. While saving, the same workflow star is disabled in both grids. If saving fails, a message asks you to refresh to check the saved state. Search also filters the Favorites section. Removing the final favorite hides the section; the workflow remains in the main grid.

## BI assignments
Enable/Disable actions sit beside Edit and Delete in the Actions column on both assignment lists. The Enabled column displays the saved status. Changes require confirmation; disabled assignments retain their settings.
- /help/bi-audience-assignment — Home-page audiences, paged user search, User/Role/current Business Unit, enabled grants and presentation.
- /help/bi-data-view-assignment — Concrete published Table View bindings, Records/Dashboard mode, named Dashboard tabs, independent enablement, one-time legacy expansion. View filters are not Superset row filters.

Data View Assignment list: Target shows the Function Unit name. Use each column header menu to filter, sort, move or resize columns. Enabled is filtered from its header; the toolbar has Dashboard Title and Target only.

Audience Assignment, who can do what (/help/bi-audience-assignment#permissions): not limited by team (any active Dashboard to any User, Role or Business Unit). System Administrator and every Technical Lead: New Assignment, Edit, Enable / Disable, Delete on every assignment; whether a person can open a Dashboard that carries Superset roles is decided by RBAC Mapping (System Administrator only); once opened, the embed always runs with the guest role, so RBAC Mapping does not filter what it shows. Auditor read-only (no New Assignment, no Actions column).

Data View Assignment, who can do what (/help/bi-data-view-assignment#permissions): System Administrator every assignment with New Assignment, Edit, Enable / Disable, Delete. Technical Lead only assignments of Function Units of the teams they lead; Target in the toolbar and in New Assignment offers only those Function Units (one Admin Center has no team for yet is not offered); Dashboard is any active Dashboard; row actions on those rows. Auditor every assignment read-only (no New Assignment, no Actions column); an Auditor who also leads a team gets them for that team. Saving another team's Function Unit: This belongs to team X (code), which you do not lead.

## Table Data — who can do what (/help/table-data#permissions)

The header shows Read-only access or Read/write access; a lock marks read-only tables in the Function Units panel. Read-only keeps Search and Export CSV and hides Add, Export Template, Import, the Active / Inactive buttons for checked records and the row actions. System Administrator: every deployed table, read/write. Technical Lead: Common tables and tables linked to at least one Function Unit of a team they lead; read/write only when every linked Function Unit belongs to a team they lead; Common tables and tables also linked to another team's Function Unit or to one without a team are read-only (System Administrator changes them); a shared table is also listed under the other team's Function Unit. Auditor: every table, read-only; an Auditor who leads a team changes that team's tables. In Add and Edit a Lookup column can search the table it points to even when that table is not listed.

## Environment variables — who can do what (/help/environment-variables#permissions)

Only a System Administrator adds, edits or deletes variables. Technical Lead and Auditor: same list read-only, no Add variable, no Actions column (Edit, Delete). Value / secret path: TEXT shows the current value, or the default when blank, for every role; VAULT shows the stored secret path to a System Administrator and only Configured / Not configured to everyone else.

## Table Structure (/help/relation-table-structure)

Admin Center → Relation Tables → Table Structure defines Relation Tables; records are on /help/table-data. A table linked to no Function Unit is Common. Order: Create Table → Display Name, Function Unit, Field Definitions → Create Table → Deploy on the row → More → Access and Portal on for User Portal.

List: Function Unit panel (All Function Units, Common, each Function Unit with count); Search... matches Display Name; Export (checked rows or current page). Columns Display Name, Version (v0 before first Deploy), Status (INIT never deployed; DEPLOYED, the only status offered in User Portal and drawn on the ER diagram; UPDATED changed after Deploy, also by ER diagram Save; ROLLBACK; UPDATED and ROLLBACK leave User Portal and the ER diagram until the next Deploy, Table Data lists DEPLOYED, UPDATED and ROLLBACK; DRAFT only in the filter), Enable (off: not on Table Data or User Portal), Portal (on: User Portal Relation Tables for roles in Access while Status is DEPLOYED and Enable is on), Created At, Updated At. Actions: Edit / View, Deploy (Confirm Deploy; next version, Change Log Initial deployment / Structure update deployment; adds missing audit fields), Version (Version History; Rollback restores that version's field list — names, types, length, DECIMAL precision and scale, Nullable, Primary Key, Default Value, display names — as a new version, Status ROLLBACK; foreign keys, Lookup Settings, PK generation and formulas are cleared and must be set again), More (ER Diagram, Compare Added/Removed/Modified/Unchanged, Rollback, Access, Delete). View ER Diagram: tables with Status DEPLOYED you can see; Save writes back only the tables whose foreign keys changed, and is hidden when a change would touch a table you cannot edit; a saved table becomes UPDATED and leaves the diagram and User Portal until it is deployed again.

Form (Create / Edit Table Structure): Display Name required; Table Name generated from display name, platform-wide unique; Description; Function Unit multi-select or Common (mutually exclusive; blank saves as Common for a System Administrator; required for a Technical Lead, placeholder Select Function Unit(s) of your teams). Field Definitions: Display Name, Field Name (required), Type VARCHAR/INTEGER/BIGINT/DECIMAL/BOOLEAN/DATE/TIMESTAMP/TEXT/LOOKUP, Length (255), Nullable (on), Primary Key + Strategy (Manual, UUID default, Auto increment, Prefixed sequence, Date + daily sequence, Date + monthly sequence, Custom format; see /help/table-design#pk), Foreign Key (Reference Table with Status DEPLOYED, Reference Primary Key Fields), Lookup (LOOKUP only), Computed (not on audit/key/FK/LOOKUP; /help/computed-fields#relation), Default Value. Audit fields created_at, created_by, updated_at, updated_by: added on Deploy, locked. Lookup Settings: Reference Table, Search Fields, Display Fields, Label Field, Allow multiple, Show backfill panel (default on), Fixed Filters (Equals/Contains/Starts with/Ends with), Derived / Cascade (Driven by field, Behavior Auto-fill / Filter only, Join Columns). Access Config: Add Role (Permission Read & Write / Readonly; BU Role tab Business Unit + roles; System Role tab), Role, Type, Permission, Created At, Created By, Delete.

Who can do what (#permissions): System Administrator every table, all actions, any Function Unit or Common. Technical Lead sees Common tables and tables linked to at least one Function Unit of a team they lead (panel lists only their teams' Function Units); changes a table only when every linked Function Unit is their team's; Create Table offers only their teams' Function Units, Common greyed out, at least one required; Reference Table lists only visible tables. Auditor every table read-only (no Create Table, View on every row); an Auditor who leads a team changes that team's tables. Read-only table (#read-only): Edit becomes View, form titled View Table Structure; form and Field Definitions grid read-only (no Add Field, no bin icon, no Save Changes); Deploy, Rollback, Delete hidden; Enable and Portal locked; Version History without Rollback; Access Config without Add Role / Delete. A shared table shows the other team's Function Unit name; it cannot be opened or changed there.

Fail: Display name is required; Table name "…" already exists platform-wide; Please add at least one field / All fields must have a name; Link the table to at least one function unit of a team you lead (form check under Function Unit when a Technical Lead saves without one of their teams' Function Units; a direct API call gets the server wording Link the relation table to at least one function unit of a team you lead); This belongs to team X (code), which you do not lead / This is shared by every team … only a System Administrator can change it (the pages hide such actions; only from a page opened before access changed, or a direct API call); not on Table Data (INIT or Enable off); Failed to load table structures.

## LDAP Sync Records (/help/ac-audit-ldap-sync)

Admin Center → Audit Log → LDAP Sync Records. One row per LDAP / AD sync run, newest first; read-only for System Administrator, Technical Lead and Auditor, who all see the same records (not filtered by team). No button to start, stop or delete a run; only a System Administrator can start a sync, through the API only (no button anywhere in Admin Center).

Columns: Type — Users (full), Users (incremental) (only entries changed since the last Users (full) or Users (incremental) run that ended Succeeded, Partly succeeded runs and group runs do not count; with none it runs as Users (full); user runs happen only when a System Administrator starts them), Groups (full), Groups (incremental) (bring virtual-group lists in line with mapped AD groups; start-up and scheduled runs are recorded as Groups (incremental); a System Administrator can start any of the four types through the API only). Status — Running; Succeeded (user run read to the end and stored every entry with an employee ID; group run read every mapped AD group in full and stored every member with an employee ID, empty or missing AD groups and the System Administrators keep-members guard included; entries without an employee ID are skipped and do not change the status); Partly succeeded (user run: some entries with an employee ID could not be stored and the others were, and the next Users (incremental) starts from the last Succeeded Users run, not this one; group run: some AD groups Not read or Read incompletely, nobody removed from their lists, the rest synced); Failed (group run could read no AD group, nothing changed; user run read the directory but could store none of the entries with an employee ID — Added and Updated 0, Message Could not be stored — and the next Users (incremental) starts from the last Succeeded Users run; or any run stopped on an error). Started (browser time zone). Duration (12.3s, 2m 05s; dash when not finished or not recorded). Fetched. Added · Updated (user accounts created / updated; dash when not finished or an older record without them). Failed items (entries with an employee ID that could not be stored, e.g. a database error; the Admin Center log names them). Skipped items (entries without an employee ID: not stored by design, not failures, no effect on status; in a group run an account in two mapped AD groups counts twice, as in Fetched; dash for an older record). Message — failure text as recorded, cut at 1,000 characters, may name an LDAP host or DN, never passwords; hover a cut-off Message to read it all, one note per line; group runs list Not read, lists unchanged / Read incompletely, nobody removed / No members found (missing or empty AD group) / Kept the AD members of …: removing them would leave no active member (only the System Administrators group has this guard) / No virtual group maps an AD group; any run that read the directory: Skipped without an employee ID (not stored): N; Users runs: Could not be stored: N (not the starting point of the next incremental sync).

Find: search box Search type, status, message or groups matches Message, the AD groups read (not a column) and stored codes such as FAILED or HERMES_AD_GROUP; column header menu sorts, filters (Type and Status by label), moves, resizes; Export downloads checked rows or the current page; Refresh. Members a group run added or removed are separate entries in Admin Center Audit Logs with Operator LDAP_SYNC_JOB; members added by hand are never removed by a sync.

When syncs run: only while ldap.enabled and ldap.sync-enabled are both on; a group sync once after Admin Center starts and on ldap.sync-cron (default every 2 hours, on the hour); one LDAP sync at a time across instances, a manual start while a start-up, scheduled or manual sync runs returns HTTP 409 Another LDAP sync is running (also for one minute after a start-up or scheduled run started); a start-up or scheduled run skips, not queues, when another sync runs, and Admin Center logs a warning; a run keeps the lock for as long as it takes, and if Admin Center stops during a run the lock is released within 20 minutes; when Redis (which holds the lock) cannot be reached a manual start returns HTTP 503 The LDAP sync did not start: its lock service (Redis) cannot be reached. Try again later, or ask the platform operator to check Redis.

Fail: no records (LDAP sync switched off — ldap.enabled and ldap.sync-enabled — or not run yet); Running long after Started (the run did not finish, e.g. Admin Center restarted); Failed (read Message; Could not be stored with Added and Updated 0 = a Users run stored nothing, see the Admin Center log; the group sync retries on schedule); Partly succeeded (group run: Message names the AD groups not read or read in part, the next run retries them; Users run: some entries could not be stored, see the Admin Center log, the next Users (incremental) reads again from the last Succeeded Users run); 409 on a manual start (another sync is running); 503 on a manual start (Redis, which holds the sync lock, cannot be reached; nothing started); Failed to load LDAP sync records (Refresh); menu missing (not System Administrator, Auditor or Technical Lead of an active team).
